description: Little Theo is drifting off to sleep when he is frightened by a hooting sound. His father shows him how to overcome his fear by naming it. title: TransFabulous: Intuitive Painting
description: In this workshop, the focus is all about feeling! Painting can be a daunting thing if you are not a self-proclaimed 'artist,' but this workshop turns that concept on its head! What do you feel in the moment, and how do your hands translate that onto a canvas? Participants will be asked to intuitively paint what they hear in the music provided by the program, focusing on sensation rather than the technical skill and aesthetic outcome. 8x10" canvases, acrylic paints, oil pastels, brushes, and related supplies will be provided. Leo or 'Inkblot' is a self-taught and supported local painter, illustrator, and writer whose artistic focus is mindfulness, self-expression, and pushing the limits of color, composition, and message. After years of studying technical skill in penciling and line art illustration, Inkblot's new artistic goal is to break the aesthetic molds of art through intuitive and therapeutic techniques; and to spread the message that anyone can create art without the pressure of technical perfection! All are welcome to this trans-centered space. TransFabulous and TransPractical are each a series of workshops led by artists and educators who identify as transgender (trans) or gender non-conforming (GNC) – TransFabulous provides an outlet through artistic creation while TransPractical addresses applied aspects of the trans/GNC experience. Sponsor: Friends of the Hennepin County Library.

title: Protection Charm With Traditional Korean Patchwork
description: These classes center on the theme, "The Art of Being With...," and are related to the exhibit at Minneapolis Central Library. Together, they explore the idea that giving and receiving care and love brings meaning to our lives. Thoughtfulness is essential in finding purpose; without it, everyday moments can feel less significant. Rather than focusing on technical skills, each class highlights the meaningful act of creating objects that reflect care. Participants will work with ceramic painting and traditional textile elements to practice thoughtfulness and express care for themselves and others. No previous experience is needed; all skill levels are welcome. In session one of the two-part series, participants will paint and work with textiles. In session two, textile work will be incorporated and ceramic pieces will be painted and assembled into the finished object. Materials provided. Register for both sessions. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund. September 12 : Painting on ceramic pollack + sewing Jogakbo. Cultural significance: In a custom called Bugeo Aekmaegi, dried pollack uses its wide-open eyes and mouth to watch for evil spirits and swallow misfortune. This is paired with Jogakbo (patchwork), the traditional Korean art of "wrapping luck" and fortune. September 26 : Painting on ceramic old coin + sewing Jogakbo. Cultural significance: These represent Byeoljeon, rare commemorative coins gifted by mothers to marrying daughters on decorative key pendants to wish for marital harmony and prosperity. This is paired with Jogakbo patchwork to wrap and hold that family fortune together. View The Art of Being With: Light, Shadow, Wind and Body exhibit – on display August 8-September 27 in Cargill Gallery on the second floor of Minneapolis Central Library.

Hayden Heights Library in the Park: Stories, Songs, and More brings beloved library programs outdoors with an ukulele storytime with Miss Rose, bubbles, crafts, and a cool treat from Sweet Fruci’s Frozen Delights—plus a visit from the Mobile Library where you can check out books, get a card, and more. This event is part of Saint Paul Public Library’s continued commitment to the Hayden Heights community during the library renovation. Free and all are welcome—drop in anytime between 10 a.m.

title: Neighborhood Architecture: Irvine Park Saint Paul
description: Jeanne Kosfeld and Richard Kronick have created a unique first book featuring the lovely Irvine Park neighborhood. Readers may color or paint eighteen sketches of old homes while learning about the area’s history and architecture. The book’s author, Richard Kronick, will speak about the history of Irvine Park. If weather permits, this talk will be followed by a short walk from the library to Irvine Park, where Mr. Kronick will give a 50-minute tour of the neighborhood. Please register if you will be taking the walking tour. Registration is not required for the talk.
